milestones.title: Platform qualification and contracts
milestones.description: Qualify exact initial server/notebook profiles; record hardware, firmware and artifact constraints; establish versioned native interfaces and reproducible evidence before implementation claims.

milestones.title: Original kernel and native services
milestones.description: Boot the original x86-64 kernel, implement isolation, scheduling and registered asynchronous channels, and run native services through a documented SDK.

milestones.title: Native devices and installation
milestones.description: Implement native physical-device support, storage, networking, secure channels and installation; qualify the exact wired mains-powered notebook independently.

milestones.title: Native CUDA execution and inference
milestones.description: Initialize selected NVIDIA hardware, execute exact-target device-only cubins, implement the required CUDA Driver API subset, and qualify one model architecture/precision with native execution.

milestones.title: Native transport and cluster control
milestones.description: Qualify an independently implemented pinned Homa version, bounded transfers and collectives; implement authenticated membership, three-node quorum, measured admission and native model/task APIs.

milestones.title: Four-device distributed inference product
milestones.description: Demonstrate three stable workers plus one native-OS notebook executing resident shards, independently feasible prefill/decode handoff, tenant isolation, failure semantics, signed recovery and measured service results.

milestones.title: Cloud and geographic operation
milestones.description: Qualify named cloud profiles separately for native boot, permitted networking and accelerator execution; implement regional locality and explicitly measured remote work/state movement.

milestones.title: Bounded recursive software improvement
milestones.description: Generate and evaluate compute/runtime/driver/kernel candidates under independent evaluation, promotion and recovery authority; preserve provenance and held-out evidence.

milestones.title: AArch64 and native Apple M5
milestones.description: Port the original core, qualify exact Apple M5 platform/boot, implement independent Apple GPU execution and inference, and separately qualify native Thunderbolt transport.

milestones.title: Additional backend and compatibility programs
milestones.description: Individually qualify broader CUDA ecosystem compatibility, direct GPU/NIC DMA, and an optional native AMD GPU backend without expanding initial support claims.

issues.title: Qualify the first stable-node and native notebook platforms
issues.body:
## Deliverable

Produce the initial hardware qualification record before selecting advertised supported SKUs. Identify candidate modern x86-64 stable nodes and an exact wired mains-powered NVIDIA notebook, plus a recoverable laboratory target.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Record UEFI/CPU, PCIe topology, IOMMU, interrupts, storage, NIC, GPU device/ISA/firmware and notebook ACPI power prerequisites.
- [ ] Identify firmware/artifact acquisition and redistribution constraints; distinguish documented interfaces from experimental assumptions.
- [ ] Select exact initial profiles and device/compiler targets only after the critical native-access questions have evidence.
- [ ] Record support status per profile; do not treat architecture family or nameplate memory as proof of execution.

## Evidence to attach

Attach device inventories, source links, firmware versions, topology diagrams, memory estimates and the initial supported-profile decision.

Include implementation commit, exact build/run commands, artifact versions and raw reproducible results. The inventory tooling and requirements packet are implemented; physical platform qualification remains open.

issues.title: Implement address spaces, capabilities and owned memory
issues.body:
## Deliverable

Implement isolation domains, capability namespaces and physical/virtual region ownership.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Prove through negative tests that domains cannot map, read or write unauthorized regions.
- [ ] Implement allocation, delegation, sharing, bounds checking, generation checking and revocation.
- [ ] Account committed/reserved memory and prevent reuse while authorized work still owns a region.

## Accepted progress

[PR #58](https://github.com/AG187-Lab/tessryn/pull/58), merged as `3e5a1254251038d26bd2a8c77c517607d842bdea`, adds a bounded single-CPU x86_64 QEMU matrix with ten fixed CPL3 recipes: caller forgery, trusted-operation forgery, unauthorized read, read-only sharing, exact bounds, kernel isolation, data NX, recursive revocation, writable reuse and stale identities. It extends the original four-probe native slice and binds the results to the source, compiler, immutable build inputs and exact raw exception frames.

The reviewed local implementation passed 578 Python tests, 97 Rust host tests, three exact twin build pairs, ten fresh matrix boots with 52 actual CPL3 traps, the original four native-slice boots and seven K01 emulator cases. The published [evidence packet](https://github.com/AG187-Lab/tessryn/tree/709f67cd448fb8a088ac1ca5761c472656960709/evidence/k02-native-matrix) contains raw traces, manifests, verification reports, commands and hashes. Its README records the source/toolchain requirements and the distinction between the public text packet and full binary evidence. All ten PR checks passed. The [fresh Linux native-matrix CI run](https://github.com/AG187-Lab/tessryn/actions/runs/38686098668) passed, and a separate artifact audit checked exactly 198 files, both twin build pairs, all ten matrix traces and four original-slice traces, the 97 host-test receipts and source bindings. Its tested merge tree exactly matched the reviewed PR head. This portable audit does not claim to reexecute the Linux compiler on the macOS review host.

These are fixed probe programs and host ownership-policy checks. That matrix did not establish general service execution. Arbitrary-program isolation, production native services, SMP lifetime enforcement, device/DMA isolation and physical-machine qualification remain open. Complete lease checks identified as `trusted_backend` in the matrix are trusted kernel checks; the raw CPL3 faults establish only their documented mapping boundaries. The acceptance boxes above remain open for that broader deliverable.

## Single-CPU region service progress

The [resumable region service](https://github.com/AG187-Lab/tessryn/blob/main/design/k02-region-service.md) adds a reusable bounded dispatcher and two image-bound CPL3 programs that construct requests, consume replies and resume from protected contexts. Clean implementation `bf9c82528f83e25814334c696a02aff86120fa21` passed three fresh single-CPU QEMU boots: read-only sharing/write denial, owner revocation/stale-access denial, and malformed/forged/stale authority rejection with erased-page reuse. The [public evidence](https://github.com/AG187-Lab/tessryn/tree/main/evidence/k02-region-service) records 66 requests, 68 actual privilege traps, four context switches per boot, preserved GPR/legacy FP state and final zero mappings/allocations/charges. Independent twins match all ten artifacts; 21 service-policy and 97 existing Rust host tests, 658 Python tests, seven K01 boots, four original probes, the ten-case matrix and 13-case/208-sample guest benchmark regressions passed.

Caller identity comes from protected task/root state. Copied 96-byte descriptors cannot name internal leases or acknowledge quiescence; trusted teardown fences, clears PTEs, reloads CR3 and retires leases before reuse. Busy capabilities stay journaled and charged until release succeeds. The service remains cooperative, capacity-bounded and image-bound; arbitrary executable admission, timer preemption, production service isolation, SMP, physical hardware and DMA remain open. These results advance the issue without checking its broader acceptance boxes. A native performance comparison remains pending.

The separate [K03 timer profile](https://github.com/AG187-Lab/tessryn/blob/main/design/k03-timer-preemption.md) now adds bounded HPET preemption and strict CPU budgets to the same protected contexts, with [four clean accepted boots](https://github.com/AG187-Lab/tessryn/tree/main/evidence/k03-timer). The cooperative profile retains its own original scope; broader K02 isolation and lifecycle acceptance remain open.

## Evidence to attach

Attach additional mapping/capability tests, fault traces and ownership/lifetime invariants as the general service is implemented. Include the implementation commit, exact build/run commands, artifact versions and raw reproducible results.

## Design and primary references

- [Native ABI](https://github.com/AG187-Lab/tessryn/blob/main/design/native-abi.md)
- [Original kernel commitment](https://github.com/AG187-Lab/tessryn/blob/main/design/decisions/0001-original-kernel.md)
- [Native isolation decision](https://github.com/AG187-Lab/tessryn/blob/main/design/decisions/0015-native-memory-slice.md)

issues.title: Implement SMP scheduling, clocks and execution budgets
issues.body:
## Deliverable

Implement multi-core task execution, monotonic time, accounting and bounded CPU reservations.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Run isolated tasks on multiple cores with accurate accounting under contention.
- [ ] Exercise budget exhaustion, deadlines, task failure and runnable/blocked transitions.
- [x] Document enforcement limits and clock/lease assumptions without implying universal GPU or memory-bandwidth preemption.

## Single-CPU timer integration progress, October 16, 2026

The [HPET timer integration](https://github.com/AG187-Lab/tessryn/blob/main/design/k03-timer-preemption.md) connects the unchanged scheduler policy to two protected resumable CPL3 programs. Clean implementation `a2ed4cc20d148d7d9337ed815cb8d517f0dbd29d` passed independent 14-artifact twins, all 26 compiler/28 runtime bindings, 90 focused Rust host checks, 697 Python tests and four fresh original-kernel QEMU executions. The [evidence packet](https://github.com/AG187-Lab/tessryn/tree/main/evidence/k03-timer) records 41 requests, 69 actual traps, 27 authentic timer IRQs, protected context continuity, an actual pending IRQ0 drain and the bound forged INT20 #GP.

A's 80ms lifetime budget and admission-relative 100ms deadline stop further A execution while B completes. Both native stops in this packet are strict late Failed states with full actual charging and sticky domain halt; they are not relabelled exact Exhausted/DeadlineExpired stops. Host tests separately cover those exact boundary states, numerical blocked idle/no refill and stale/overflow rejection. No user request supplies identity, budget, time or stop acknowledgment. All four boots finish with zero CPU reservations/leases and memory ownership. ARM_MISSED no-entry recovery in that historical packet has host-model and synthetic-parser coverage only; no native observation is claimed there.

Fresh same-source regressions pass: 97 native host tests, four original probes, ten matrix boots/52 traps, seven K01 boots including ISO, the three cooperative service cases/21 host tests and the 13-case/208-sample guest benchmark. The benchmark's strict warnings caught and verified the fix for timer helpers leaking into another build profile. All earlier failed/dirty diagnostics remain outside acceptance.

This closes the bounded single-CPU timer integration subgate, not the SMP deliverable. The broader acceptance boxes remain open for multicore/contention execution. Physical clock and latency qualification, cross-core ownership/synchronization, general native idle/wakeup, devices/DMA and registered native performance comparisons remain pending. No physical or inference-performance claim is made.

## Two-CPU bootstrap implementation, October 17, 2026

The separate [original-kernel bootstrap profile](https://github.com/AG187-Lab/tessryn/blob/main/design/k03-smp-bootstrap.md) admits exactly two legacy xAPIC CPUs through bounded, span-validated ACPI table views and an owned handoff. Its 26 parser host tests cover malformed lengths, checksums, flags, duplicate IDs and fixed HPET metadata. The runtime implements targeted INIT/SIPI, private AP GDT/IDT/TSS and stacks with a common software-immutable CR3, 4096 atomic increments per CPU (8192 total), heartbeat progress over 20ms, three generation-bound IPIs with actual ISR/EOI acknowledgments, and a terminal stop. A separate missing_ap case deliberately omits SIPI and requires a bounded expected timeout.

Clean implementation `f3f39b8e333b5e6fcb96a829dddaa480a5858ee1` passed both fresh scenarios, six byte-identical EFI/object/disk twins, 26 Rust parser checks, 725 Python tests and independent replay of the exact 120-file artifact inventory. The [public evidence packet](https://github.com/AG187-Lab/tessryn/tree/main/evidence/k03-smp-bootstrap) retains original traces and registrations. Earlier-profile regressions passed all 51 commands at `febcb2ff53a512daa7ba8bac6f6156c9cbc3a6e4`; the final delta changes only three new SMP build helpers, with 91 declared old compiler/runtime/host inputs verified unchanged. Their actual source identities remain distinct. The budget regression additionally observes one actual ARM_MISSED no-entry stop, charging the full 1.472ms against the remaining 63us grant while the peer completes; historical packet bytes remain unchanged. All RAM stays retained; the stop does not authorize reuse. This profile adds no CPL3 SMP scheduling, shared budget/accounting enforcement, per-CPU timers, general idle/wakeup, TLB shootdown, device/DMA quiescence or physical platform/performance claim. The existing single-CPU profiles retain their original contracts. The broader acceptance boxes remain open, and a preregistered native complete-path performance comparison remains pending.

## Isolated two-CPU user contexts, October 17, 2026

The separate [CPL3 profile](https://github.com/AG187-Lab/tessryn/blob/main/design/k03-smp-user.md) now executes two isolated instances of an original image-bound program template under private immutable CR3 roots and per-CPU GDT/IDT/TSS, stacks and saved GPR/legacy FP state. SWAPGS protects the continuation even when the program reloads GS. Its rendezvous runs both user contexts with overlapping progress, yields and resumes AP, and stops both unbounded user loops through source-authenticated peer IPIs. Peer-read and forged-INT66 cases fault through private #PF/#GP boundaries while BSP user progress continues afterward.

Clean implementation `ef205654aa6b4e75afb77cc8c2affc1a927f7656` passed all three fresh original-kernel boots, nine byte-identical EFI/object/disk twins, 755 Python tests, 26 actual parser checks and all 57 earlier-profile regression commands at the same source. The [62-file text packet](https://github.com/AG187-Lab/tessryn/tree/main/evidence/k03-smp-user) retains original captures, source chains and verification receipts. Independent replay of the separate 149-file artifact checks 14 compiler/26 runtime inputs, 54 raw page walks, seven complete CPL3 register/FP frames, actual descriptor/control state, protected roots/stacks, hardware ISR/EOI and continued peer progress after both faults. All RAM remains retained; the terminal acknowledgment authorizes no reuse.

This completes a bounded per-CPU user-execution subgate. Shared scheduler ownership, aggregate budget reservations/accounting under contention, per-CPU timers, arbitrary program admission, idle/wakeup/migration, reusable quiescence, devices/DMA and physical clocks remain open. The broad K03 acceptance boxes stay unchecked; a preregistered native complete-path performance comparison remains pending.

## Evidence to attach

Attach scheduler timelines, budget tests, cross-core traces and timing assumptions.

Include implementation commit, exact build/run commands, artifact versions and raw reproducible results. Host scheduler policy, single-CPU timer integration, two-CPU bootstrap and isolated per-CPU CPL3 contexts are implemented; shared SMP scheduling, aggregate budgets/accounting under contention and physical clocks remain open.

- [Native ABI](https://github.com/AG187-Lab/tessryn/blob/main/design/native-abi.md)
